title: wcmatch: Polynomial-time ReDoS when matching untrusted names against multi-star patterns (default flags)
description:
Summary

With default flags, a pattern that contains several * wildcards takes polynomial time, O(n^k) for k stars, to reject a crafted file name. The pattern is an ordinary developer constant such as *_*_*_*_*.csv; only the string being matched comes from the attacker. A 255-byte file name (the maximum on common filesystems) takes 73 s with fnmatch.fnmatch() and 86 s with glob.globmatch(). The standard library's fnmatch handles the same input in under a millisecond.

This is different from GHSA-84v8-qmgq-9g88: that advisory covers extglob patterns, while this case needs no flags and no attacker-controlled pattern.

title: svglib: Exponential resource consumption via nested <use> references in svg2rlg
description:
Summary

svg2rlg() expands references without any limit on the total number of expansions. Only direct cycles are rejected (CircularRefError). A group containing N elements that point to another such group multiplies the work by N per nesting level, so an SVG of about 1.4 KB makes svglib clone and render over 100,000 nodes, taking tens of seconds of CPU time and hundreds of MiB of memory. Each additional level adds about 245 bytes to the document and multiplies time by ~10.

title: contao/core-bundle: Non-admin users can self-grant permissions that implicitly make them administrators
description:
Commit 2b83a60f7763 (5.7.3) hardened the template editor: it added TemplateEditorModuleVoter + CheckTemplateEditorSaveListener so a non-admin cannot self-grant the tpl_editor backend module (editable PHP-capable templates permit server-side code execution). That voter supports only the modules field and the literal value tpl_editor.

The equally RCE-capable theme_import capability lives in a different field - the themes checkbox field (tl_user_group.php:98-105 options include theme_import; identical on tl_user.php:248-253) - which has no save_callback and no voter. TemplateEditorModuleVoter is the only DC voter registered for tl_user_group, and it does not cover the themes field. So a delegated user manager can add theme_import to their own (or a managed) account.

title: memtomem-stm: Concurrent LTM recovery can duplicate reconnects or reuse a cancelled transport session
description: Concurrent surfacing RPC failures can trigger more than one reconnect for the same dirty session, and cancellation during a post-reconnect retry can leave the replacement session reusable despite an interrupted protocol exchange. The private fix introduces monotonic session generations, one shielded shared reconnect flight per dirty generation, and generation-aware cancellation handling across search, access-count, and scratch RPCs. The duplicate-reconnect subcase was introduced in 0.1.24; cancellation recovery affects the broader listed range.

title: nats-server Leaf node connections bypass Nats-Trace-Dest permission check
description:
Background

NATS.io is a high performance open source pub-sub distributed communication technology, built for the cloud, on-premise, IoT and edge computing.

The NATS Server supports leafnode connections between servers and message tracing through NATS headers.

Problem Description

Message trace destination checks were applied to ordinary client connections but not consistently to messages arriving through leafnode connections.

A leafnode operator could cause trace events to be sent to subjects that would not otherwise be permitted and could use trace-only behavior to prevent normal delivery or storage of affected messages.

Trace events can include routing, subscription, account, service import and JetStream metadata. The payload of the original application message is not chosen

 case sc.XClientOn && cmdXCLIENT.match(cmd):

What the fix did and the gap

The v2.3.0 fix (commit e88dabb) routed the _select field through a strict new gate, sanitizeSelectField (postgres.go:947/1003/2097). That gate validates only the OUTERMOST function name against a 13-entry allowlist and uses a character allowlist that permits spaces, single quotes and parens. title: js-toml allows uncontrolled recursion in load() leading RangeError (stack exhaustion) on deeply nested input
description:
Summary

load() parses untrusted TOML using a recursive-descent parser (Chevrotain) and a
recursive tree-walking interpreter. Neither the parser nor the interpreter enforces a
maximum nesting / key depth. A small, attacker-controlled document with deep nesting
(arrays, inline tables) or a long dotted key drives recursion past the V8 call-stack
limit, and load() throws an uncaught RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded.

This is a problem for two reasons:

1. Denial of Service. A tiny payload (≈2 KB) reliably aborts parsing. In any

title: Refitter: Unrestricted OpenAPI references permit build-host SSRF and file inclusion
description:
Summary

Refitter (the refitter dotnet tool, built on NJsonSchema for $ref resolution) fetches remote
http(s) URLs and reads local files (including absolute paths and ../ traversal outside the input
directory), inlining the referenced schema into the generated Refit interface/contracts. Running
refitter --output Out.cs on a spec whose $ref points at an attacker/internal URL or an
arbitrary local file yields SSRF, remote file inclusion, and local file inclusion. Verified on
Refitter 2.0.0.

Details

- $ref: http://attacker-or-internal/evil.json#/... -> build host fetches (SSRF) and inlines the
 remote schema (RFI); confirmed property REMOTE_REFIT_PROP.
- $ref: /abs/path.json#/... or ../../secret.json#/... -> out-of-tree local file read + inlined
 (LFI);

description:
Summary

The Appium storage plugin exposes an HTTP endpoint POST /storage/delete that takes a user-supplied name and deletes it from the server storage folder. The handler passes name straight into path.join(storageRoot, name) and then fs.rimraf() without any path sanitization. By sending a name containing ../ sequences, an unauthenticated remote client can escape the storage root and recursively delete arbitrary files and directories that the Appium process user can write, anywhere on the host filesystem.

The same plugin's *upload* path validates the name via fs.sanitizeName (requireValidItemOptions), but the *delete* path does not an asymmetry that makes the missing validation unambiguous.

title: OliveTin: Second-Order OS Command Injection via shellAfterCompleted
description:
Summary

OliveTin's shellAfterCompleted post-execution hook injects unsanitized variables — including arbitrary command output (output), the authenticated username (ot_username), and the exit code (exitCode) — directly into a shell command template processed by sh -c. Unlike the main action's argument handling, no checkShellArgumentSafety validation is applied to these variables. An attacker who can influence the output of a command (e.g., via user-supplied arguments that reflect in stdout, or through trusted-header username spoofing) can inject arbitrary OS commands into the post-execution shell.

description:
A path traversal vulnerability was identified in mail-parser when extracting email attachments using the write_attachments() and write_sample() APIs.

A specially crafted email containing malicious attachment filenames (for example, using directory traversal sequences such as "../" or absolute filesystem paths) could cause files to be written outside the intended output directory. Depending on how the library was used and the permissions of the executing process, this could result in arbitrary file overwrite.

The vulnerability affects mail-parser versions 3.8.0 through 4.5.0.

The issue has been addressed by introducing comprehensive filename sanitization and path validation before any file is written to disk. The fix includes:

title: Nuxt payload URL generation has quadratic cost for repeated slashes in the request path

Summary

Nuxt strips trailing slashes from the request path with a regular expression whose cost grows quadratically with the length of a run of consecutive slashes. A single unauthenticated request with a long run of slashes can occupy the server's event loop for a noticeable time, delaying every other request handled by the same process.

When a page is rendered with payload extraction (any route covered by an isr, swr or cache route rule), Nuxt builds the _payload.json URL from the raw request path. title: Nuxt: Incomplete fix for GHSA-6gq8-jgmh-3ffp: an encoded slash (%2F) in the request path bypasses route rules on catch-all page routes
description:
Summary

Nuxt matches route rules against the request path with encoded slashes (%2F) left encoded, while the page router decodes them into route params. A request that spells a slash as %2F can therefore render a page through a catch-all route without the route rules configured for the path it resolves to. Impact

An unauthenticated attacker can bypass route rules that protect paths served by a catch-all page route, or by a custom route whose param can span several segments.

title: AIOHTTP: Event loop stall in add_domain() wildcard matching
description:
Summary

Application.add_domain() compiled each * in a host mask to [^:]*. With two or more wildcards in a mask, matching a long Host header that does not match the mask took polynomial time on the event loop.

Impact

An attacker could stall a server that registers a domain mask with more than one wildcard by sending requests with a long Host header.

Workaround

Use at most one * in a domain mask.

Patch: https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/c6ac0e44c3c573ff9616f4a6a532992538b31e43

Set-Cookie parsing created additional cookies from unrecognised name=value attributes, and CookieJar had no limit on the number of cookies stored or sent. A server could make the client store a very large number of cookies and generate very large Cookie headers.

title: AIOHTTP: Base64 multipart parts bypass client_max_size
description:
Summary

When reading a multipart part with Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64, BodyPartReader.read_chunk() kept reading until the chunk length was a multiple of 4, with no byte limit. A part with a short Content-Length, or a long run of whitespace, could cause the entire remaining body to be read into memory within a single call before any size check, or spin on the event loop.

Impact

An attacker could bypass client_max_size to cause excessive memory use, or block the event loop, with a specially crafted multipart request to any handler that reads multipart data.

Patch: https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/a555ab698e08e9baea7386d5b4c0761cb8956fdd

title: AIOHTTP: WebSocket max_msg_size bypass via integer overflow
description:
Summary

The max_msg_size check in the WebSocket reader added the declared frame length to the size of the partial message already buffered. In the C extension this addition is 64-bit arithmetic, so a declared length close to 2**63 overflowed and the check passed.

Impact

An attacker could bypass max_msg_size and cause unbounded memory use by streaming an oversized WebSocket message after a small non-final fragment.

Workaround

If unable to upgrade, the Python reader is unaffected and can be used with AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS=1.

Patch: https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/8cfbe9abe5e11b84006a10f9bdf82bf607671dab

title: AIOHTTP: Pure-Python parser request replay and buffer growth behind a declined upgrade
description:
Summary

When the pipelined request queue was full, the pure-Python parser stored the unparsed remainder internally and also returned it to the caller. After a handler declined an upgrade request, the buffered data was re-fed, so the buffer grew with each handled request and already-handled requests were dispatched to the application again.

Impact

If users are using the Python parser (AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS, or not a standard wheel installed), an attacker could cause excessive memory use and cause pipelined requests to be processed more than once.

Workaround

Switch to the default C parser.

Patch: https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/47babd8c23ca79e2bae6cc8dcb5752b61e369fc7

title: AIOHTTP: Concatenated compressed streams cause excessive CPU use
description:
Summary

When decompressing a payload made up of many concatenated compressed members (gzip, deflate or zstd), each member was decoded by passing the entire remaining input to a new decompressor, resulting in quadratic CPU time. Empty members produce no output, so client_max_size and output backpressure did not limit the work.

Impact

An attacker could block the event loop of a server with a specially crafted compressed request body or WebSocket message. A malicious server could do the same to a client.

Patch: https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/d925a80539ffd227da1d93ab4a5bff123cc777db

title: AIOHTTP: WebSocket receive queue limits bypassed by small or compressed messages
description:
Summary

The WebSocket reader continued parsing frames already received after the receive queue had paused the transport, and empty messages were not counted towards the queue size. With permessage-deflate, a single read of compressed frames could add many megabytes of decompressed messages to the queue.

Impact

An attacker could cause excessive memory use in a WebSocket server, or a malicious server against a client, by sending many small or compressed messages faster than the application consumes them.

Patch: https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/0ae507423f681161efa77d20052b4054397c7fb6

title: NLTK: Symlink escape in chat80.sql_query bypasses the pathsec data-root sandbox to read out-of-root SQLite databases
description:
Summary

nltk.sem.chat80.sql_query() opens a SQLite database by handing the result of nltk.data.find(dbname) straight to sqlite3.connect() without the path-containment check that the NLTK data sandbox (nltk.pathsec) is meant to enforce. nltk.data.find() applies only lexical checks to the resource name and returns a FileSystemPathPointer whose path is normalized with os.path.abspath but never resolved for symlinks. As a result, an in-root symbolic link that points at a SQLite file outside every registered NLTK data root is followed by SQLite, and the caller receives query results from the out-of-sandbox database.
